problem: Consider the linear transformation $T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}2x-y+z \\ -6x+3y-3z \\ 4x-2y+2z\end{aligned}]$ and the vector $\,u=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ k\end{aligned}].$ Find the value of $\,k\,$ such that $\,u\in \text{Ker}(T).$

examples.worked_solution:
A vector $\mathbf{u}$ belongs to the kernel of a linear transformation $\mathbf{T}$ if $\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{u})=\mathbf{0}.$ 

So, we need to solve the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(u) & =0 \\ [\begin{aligned}3\cdot k+12\cdot 2-3\cdot 6 \\ -2\cdot k+4\cdot 2-2\cdot 6 \\ 6\cdot k-3\cdot 2+3\cdot 6\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}3k+6 \\ -2k-4 \\ 6k+12\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we get the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}3k+6=0 \\ -2k-4=0 \\ 6k+12=0.\end{aligned}
$$

The solution to all three of these equations is $k=-2.$

feedback.problem:
Consider the linear transformation 
$T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}2x-4y+4z \\ -5x+10y-3z \\ 0\end{aligned}]$ 
and the vectors 
${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}10 \\ 5 \\ 3\end{aligned}],{v}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$
Which of the given vectors belong to $\text{Ker}(T)?$
feedback.worked_solution:
A vector $u$ belongs to the kernel of a linear transformation $T$ if $T(u)=0.$ 

Therefore, we need to compute $T({v}_{i})$ for each ${v}_{i}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}T({v}_{1}) & =T([\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 12 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ T({v}_{2}) & =T([\begin{aligned}10 \\ 5 \\ 3\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}12 \\ -9 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ T({v}_{3}) & =T([\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Since $\,T({v}_{3})=0,$ we conclude that the only vector that belongs to the kernel of $\,T$ is $\,{v}_{3}.$
